source.title: Machine Unlearning for Masked Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Georu Lee; Seungwon Jeong; Hoki Kim; Jinseong Park; Woo-Jin Lee

record.tranche_reason: Tests unlearning outcomes in the new setting of masked diffusion language models, reporting target-forgetting and utility measures. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates forgetting and retained capability, but does not fine-tune unlearned models on recovery data, ablate an activation direction, quantize weights, or test prompt-based recovery. Its KL and token-category analyses describe the proposed unlearning objective and its effects; they do not test whether supposedly forgotten knowledge can be recovered. No chance-level reference is reported for the tabulated forget metrics.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (masked diffusion LMs LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B), the study reports forget-set and retained-utility scores after unlearning on TOFU and RWKU. These bear on the 'forgets while keeping ability' part of A. No recovery attacks (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, prompting) are run, so the attack-resistance part of A and versions B–F are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: MDU, an MDLM-specific KL-to-prompt-masked-anchor objective, improves the forget–retain trade-off over AR-derived baselines on TOFU and RWKU with LLaDA and Dream. The authors name robustness to privacy attacks, larger forget sets and more models as future work.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces an MDLM-specific forward-KL objective that moves prompt-conditional predictions toward a frozen prompt-masked anchor, with temperature τ and an optional retain loss; also adapts autoregressive unlearning baselines to MDLM training losses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported forget–utility trade-off changes across τ and between the TOFU and RWKU datasets and the two model backbones.

fits_no_version.finding: Token-level conditional-vs-prompt-masked KL on stored-knowledge tokens drops only 20.6% after MDU (2.67 to 2.12), so much of the prompt-conditional signal remains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level forgetting can coexist with largely retained prompt-conditional knowledge signal in the model's predictive distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Qualitative τ=1 outputs partly leak target facts. Examples: 'Kongzi' for Confucius's real name, and the correct birth year 1951 for Rajeev Majumdar. MDU often gives fluent wrong substitutes rather than removal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregate forget metrics can hide partial factual leakage after unlearning.

record.problems: No recovery attacks or post-unlearning access tests; no chance-level reference for the forget scores; the reported tables provide no uncertainty estimates. RWKU results are averages over ten target subjects.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted TOFU RougeL and other split metrics (retain RougeL, Real-Authors and World-Facts), RWKU F-L2/F-L3, Neighbor, TruthfulQA and TriviaQA results, and GA/NPO values for RWKU metrics other than F-L1 and MMLU. These are in Tables 2 and 3. Also omitted the remaining baseline methods in those tables; the paper reports no recovery-attack results to include.

untested.parts: Resistance to simple recovery attacks (relearning, ablation, quantization, prompting). Only benchmark-internal rephrased probes (RWKU F-L3) are reported.
All: no activation-direction ablation or block-vs-delete analysis of representations.
All: no jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attempts.
All: MDU makes no robustness claim against recovery attacks.

missing.what: RWKU F-L3 (rephrased, out-of-template adversarial questions) forget scores. MDU LLaDA 0.015–0.091 vs base 0.469; Dream 0.218–0.305 vs 0.457. This is the closest result to a rephrasing probe bearing on A's 'simple attacks' part.
TOFU forget RougeL. MDU reaches about 0.000 on both models (LLaDA τ≤0.25, Dream all τ), vs base 0.380/0.865.
Real-Authors and World-Facts utility, which stay near base across the τ sweep.

record.verdict_notes: Method paper with no recovery attacks, so it cannot speak to the shallow-unlearning recovery versions B–F. Two comparator rows had the Real-Authors column read as retain (T-L-GA-RP, T-L-NPO-RP). Uncertainty is not reported and RWKU results are averaged over 10 entities. The TOFU Base SFT was created by heavy fine-tuning: 1000 epochs for LLaDA, 300 for Dream.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures targeted-knowledge scores and retained utility, but does not establish a chance-level benchmark or test whether simple attacks recover knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no test showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No post-unlearning prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
No robustness evaluation against the listed recovery attacks.
